newsitem.title: USA: Indianapolis under gun to decide on new arena.
newsitem.headline: Indianapolis under gun to decide on new arena.

text.p: Indianapolis officials are facing a tight time frame for deciding whether to offer public financing for a new arena for the Indiana Pacers basketball team, a city official said Tuesday.

Jim Snyder, special counsel to Mayor Stephen Goldsmith, said officials would have to decide soon whether they are willing to help finance a $150 million to $175 million arena or face losing the team to another city.
He said construction on a new arena would have to begin by the middle of next year in order to be completed for the 1999 basketball season.
To meet that schedule, the arena design phase would have to be started next month, he added.

With that in mind, Snyder said the city planned to immediately begin to solicit imput from corporations and citizens on whether they would support a new arena to replace Market Square Arena built in 1974.
The process began Monday night when a capital improvement board charged by Goldsmith to study the stadium issue made its presentation to the city-county council.
Snyder said while a hike in local property taxes was "off the table," the city would consider things such as ticket taxes and car rental fees to back tax-exempt revenue bonds for the project.

A "significant contribution" would also be expected from the Pacers, according to Snyder. Team officials Monday night told the city-county council they expect to lose $17 million this year and between $10 million to $11 million each of the next two years, Snyder said.
Money for the arena would also be sought from the state of Indiana, he added.
